Subject: Private hosting: operator responsibilities and MSA redlines

Rafael — thanks for the demo last week. We are moving fast on the procurement side and need to lock down two things before purchasing: (1) exact operator responsibilities/access for a private hosting (VPC) deployment, and (2) the MSA/Order Form redlines that govern snapshot handover, forensic access, and operator console access.

High level constraints from our side:
- We cannot give remote root-level access to vendor operators; any operator access must be scoped and logged, ideally read-only for most actions.
- Snapshots of customer data may only be transferred under escrow-like procedures and with customer approval and notification.
- We will require SOC 2 evidence and an agreed audit window prior to go-live.

Can you share your proposed operator responsibilities doc and a redline version of the MSA that addresses (a) operator access boundary, (b) snapshot/handback procedure, (c) evidence that demonstrates proof-of-access? It would be helpful to have a target timeline — were trying to get legal signoff by the end of next week.

Also looping Rajiv (our cloud ops lead) who will have technical follow-ups.

Thanks,

Rafael / team — reviewed the annotated MSA and operator stewardship draft. Below are the three priority redlines I recommend we send to MedGenix, plus suggested language snippets. Ive attached a short proof-of-access checklist we can share.

1) Operator Access Boundary (Section 4.2 - "Vendor Access")
Suggested: "Vendor operations staff shall be granted the minimum set of permissions necessary to perform the Services. Vendor agents will not be granted interactive shell or root privileges on Customer resources unless expressly agreed in writing for a pre-scheduled remediation session. All vendor actions shall be authenticated, logged, and made available to Customer upon request within five (5) business days."

Rationale: aligns with their "no remote root" requirement and provides a short SLA for log delivery.

2) Snapshot Handover & Chain-of-Custody (New Exhibit X)
Suggested: "Snapshots classified as Customer Data may be exported only pursuant to a signed Transfer Certificate executed by authorized representatives of both parties. The Transfer Certificate will list the snapshot identifier, transfer date/time, purpose, and receiving location. Vendor shall retain transfer logs and checksum records for 180 days and shall not use snapshot data for any purpose other than stated in the Transfer Certificate."

Rationale: Provides an "escrow-like" procedural control without conceding broad custody rights.

3) Proof-of-Access & Audit Evidence (Section 7.1 - "Audit Rights")
Suggested: "Vendor shall provide Customer with access logs, redacted session transcripts, and SOC 2 Type II reports on request. For higher-assurance reviews, Vendor will make available a time-limited observed session during which Customer's designated ops representative may observe an operator action; such sessions will be scheduled at least five (5) business days in advance and recorded for audit purposes with Customer consent."

Timing / next steps: I can draft the formal redline to the MSA by EOD Friday (6/18). Priyom — please confirm by EOD that the Transfer Certificate and observed-session process are operationally doable. Stephanie — If you can confirm availability for Thu 6/17 morning PT this morning that would be great (or propose alternatives).

Attached: MEDGENIX_ProofOfAccess_Checklist.xlsx
